title: Ben Rachumi

paragraphs: [Nazir 13a](https://www.sefaria.org/Nazir.13a.9-10) mentions Ben Rachumi asking Abaye about “I undertake to be a nazir when I have a son,” etc., and “Or perhaps he means: I love you as yourself.” Since Hyman finds no other mention of him in the Talmud, he thinks the name Ben Rachumi probably comes from the question described here as one he asked his father: “Or perhaps I love you.” In [Pesachim 39a](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.39a.11), Rav Rachumi raises a difficulty against Abaye.[^4]

notes.text: The earlier English draft and its notes were cut off; the complete frozen Hebrew is translated here. The source first says he asked Abaye but later prints מאביו, of his father. That difference remains open; it does not establish that Abaye was his father. Nazir 13a confirms the question and the phrase about loving the other person as oneself.

No new primary scalar was supplied here. The earlier Nazir 13a consultation gives Ben Rachumi asking Abaye, while the supplied later מאביו means of his father. Reading that later form as מאביי is a plausible proposed emendation, not a demonstrated vav/yod error from another entry's letter pattern. The body therefore keeps of his father explicitly as supplied, without identifying Abaye as his father. Hyman's no-other-mention assertion and LIKELY name-from-question explanation remain attributed to him, not a new global absence search or admitted etymology. Rav Rachumi in Pesachim remains a separate comparison; the earlier truncated English and notes are preserved, not reused.

Hyman’s print reads “asked Abaye” both times. The supplied Hebrew has “asked his father” the second time. The passage at Nazir 13a and its continuation on 13b address how a second speaker’s vow relates to the birth of a son. Pesachim 39a separately names Rav Rachumi in a question about bitter herbs. The suggestion about Ben Rachumi’s name is Hyman’s inference.

The [Ben Rachumi entry in Seder HaDorot](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=751&lang=en) likewise says that he asked Abaye. In the linked Nazir discussion, “I love you” is what a hypothetical second speaker might mean by joining the first speaker’s vow.
